title: Stack buffer overflow in LittleCMS K-preserving CMYK transforms
summary: A carefully crafted malicious CMYK output profile can trigger a stack buffer overflow in black-preserving CMYK-to-CMYK transforms using LittleCMS-specific intents. The maintainer says it cannot be triggered through image-embedded profiles or RGB workflows; the attacker must get a malicious output profile installed, and practical exploitation is extremely unlikely. Whether the overflow could realistically yield code execution is not established.
ai_role: The Little-CMS maintainer says the issue was discovered by Claude and Ada Logics and found by Anthropic agents studying open-source security. Ada Logics manually verified the issue and collaborated on the fix. The model/version and exact investigative steps are not stated.
classification_note: The maintainer issue is a public disclosure; it does not establish exploitation in the wild or zero-day status.
remediation_note: The maintainer-linked commit explicitly fixes issue #577. No fixed release version is stated in the issue or commit reviewed.

impacts.conditions: Requires a malicious CMYK output profile installed on the target and a black-preserving CMYK-to-CMYK transform using LittleCMS-specific intents; the maintainer says embedded image profiles and RGB workflows do not trigger it.
impacts.exploitation: The issue calls the overflow technically exploitable but says real-world exploitation is extremely improbable; it expressly says whether it could realistically lead to code execution is unclear.
